findings.label: public_id discarded
findings.detail: uploadImageToCloudinary returns publicId but submitInspection only destructures secureUrl, because the generated add_order_inspection Args type (p_notes, p_order_id, p_phase, p_photo_path) has no p_public_id. order_inspections.public_id will be null for all new Cloudinary photos. To populate it, extend the add_order_inspection RPC to accept p_public_id (DB change, out of scope for this client-side batch) and pass it through here.

findings.label: Orphaned Cloudinary asset on RPC failure
findings.detail: The previous Supabase storage.remove rollback on RPC failure is gone (as the task required, since unsigned uploads cannot be deleted from the browser). A photo that reaches Cloudinary but fails add_order_inspection now stays in Cloudinary with no DB row and no client-side way to remove it. Consider a server-side sweeper using CLOUDINARY_API_KEY/SECRET to reap uploaded-but-unreferenced assets, consistent with the cleanup strategy already described in system_architecture_rb_autoluxe.md.

findings.label: Raw Cloudinary error shown to technician
findings.detail: On a non-2xx response the helper appends the raw response body (Cloudinary's JSON error) to the thrown message, which surfaces as the user-facing error string. A technician sees raw API JSON instead of a friendly reason. Map the common Cloudinary error codes (preset misconfigured, cloud name wrong, quota exceeded) to Indonesian messages, or log the raw body and show a generic failure.
